competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Not public. Funding: USD 65M Series E led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 (CollisionWeek 18 Jul 2023). Savings claims (for example 360,000 adjuster hours at a Japanese insurer) are vendor-stated.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Low direct threat (exterior only). Possible partner or data source for triage routing. A battery module added later would be the threat.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: CCC Intelligent Solutions
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: US claims platform with AI total-loss routing; claims more than 90% accuracy (vendor). No battery-health assessment found.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Platform software; AI products about 10% of revenue per a third-party analysis of Q1 2026. US focus.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Low for Latvia. Shows insurers buy claims-workflow software, and sets the bar for integration.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: Solera / Audatex (Qapter)
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Estimating platform used by insurers and repairers, with photo AI. Only EV item found is an estimation training course (Oct 2025). Audatex Baltics UAB exists in Vilnius.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Medium as a channel. If we win a pilot, the output must integrate with or accompany the Audatex-style estimate.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: Ravin AI
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Mobile and fixed-camera vehicle inspection for insurers and fleets. Exterior, interior, tyres and glass; no battery health.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: AWS Marketplace enterprise listing USD 84,000 per 12 months for up to 20,000 inspections (about USD 4.20 per inspection, own arithmetic at full utilisation). Backers include IAG's Firemark Ventures and KAR Global (USD 15M Series A, 2023).
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Low. Useful only as evidence of subscription pricing to insurers. Not a valid anchor for a battery assessment.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: UVeye
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Drive-through camera scanning of exterior and underbody. W.R. Berkley (insurer) is a repeat investor. Cannot see battery state of health.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Per-scan price and any claims programme: not found.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Medium. It could add casing-deformation screening cheaply. A partner for the gross-damage step, not a competitor on SoH.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: AVILOO
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Austrian SoH test (about 3 minutes, compatible with over 96% of EVs) for the used-car trade. EUR 30M investment (Feb 2026). Battery warranty in 24 European markets, not Latvia, Estonia or Lithuania (renewableenergymagazine 7 Sep 2026).
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Consumer test EUR 99 (ecomento); OeAMTC Flash test EUR 69. Customers are dealers, leasing, auctions and fleets. No insurer named as a post-crash customer.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Medium threat if it extends to crash cases; most likely a partner or supplier for SoH. It measures capacity, not crash damage.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: TWAICE
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Cloud battery analytics for OEMs, fleets and storage. Munich Re's Great Lakes backs an accuracy guarantee that pays 8 times the analytics price if results fall outside the guaranteed accuracy (electrive 12 Dec 2022). It needs a telematics data stream.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Enterprise analytics. Funding includes USD 30M Series B extension (2022) and EUR 24M from the EIB (Preqin, Feb 2026, aggregator).
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Closest precedent for insurer-backed battery analytics, but for storage and fleets, not post-crash. A model for how an insurer-backed accuracy guarantee could work for us.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: Volytica and Generational
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Volytica (Dresden, Fraunhofer spin-off): charger-based tests for fleets. Generational (UK): 8,000+ assessments, average SoH 95.15%, distribution to about 6,000 UK workshops via Maverick Diagnostics.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Not public; no insurer deal found for either.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Low. Possible tool suppliers for the SoH step.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: Fraunhofer IIS AIR (X-ray)
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Drive-through X-ray of whole vehicles, about 10 min per vehicle, with auto-detection of displaced or swollen cells (electrive 22 Sep 2026). Research or pilot stage with DEKRA and Munich UAS.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: No price, no insurer customer, no deployment announced.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Long-term technology threat and potential partner. Not a Baltic option today.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: DEKRA, TUV SUD, TUV-Verband, AZT, Thatcham
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Experts and standard setters. DEKRA offers a 15-minute capacity test and damage expertise for insurers; TUV SUD offers SoH diagnosis; TUV-Verband published an assessment whitepaper (Sep 2026); AZT and Thatcham define what insurers ask for. Thatcham's Blueprint asks for open, standardised HV diagnostics on common equipment and warns against specialised subscription tools for battery removal and reinstatement.
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: No per-assessment price found for any of them.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: High in Germany and the UK, where they set methods and are trusted. Low presence in Latvia. Likely partners for method credibility and potential white-label channel. Their guidance also pressures any per-assessment price upward only if we can prove value.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: OEM assessment catalogues and dealer diagnostics (for example VW's MEB battery assessment catalogue)
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: OEMs issue their own post-crash criteria to dealers, workshops, experts and insurers. AUTOHAUS (16 Jan 2023) reports AZT's Lauterwasser saying the VW catalogue can save about EUR 10,000-30,000 per case by avoiding full HV unit replacement. [single trade-press quote, 2023].
competitors_and_alternatives.price_or_model: Bundled into dealer service; subscription portals.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Highest substitution risk. If OEMs provide the criteria, a third-party scan has less role. Dealer decisions are likely binding for warranty and liability.

competitors_and_alternatives.name: Copart UK and salvage handlers; LiBaService24; German hazard-management firms
competitors_and_alternatives.what_they_do: Copart UK runs EV storage zones, temperature sensing and trained staff (nearly 150 staff trained to IMI Levels 2-4, sponsored piece 8 Jun 2026, vendor marketing). LiBaService24 (Swiss, co-author of the SVV annex) analyses and transports damaged packs. Copart has no Baltic yards; the nearest is Finland.
competitors_and_alternatives.threat_or_partner: Partners or benchmarks for the storage and routing part of our chain. A direct competitor only if they enter the Baltics.

baltic_market: Latvia 2025 (LSM, 6 Feb 2026, trade press relaying LAA data): total premiums EUR 808m (+4.5%), claims paid EUR 476m (-1.4%), CASCO premiums EUR 138m (17% of market), OCTA premiums EUR 106m (13%). CASCO claims paid in 2024 of about EUR 86m comes from a search summary, not a fetched page, so verify on laa.lv. https://www.lsm.lv/raksts/zinas/ekonomika/06.02.2026-apdrosinasanas-tirgus-latvija-pern-audzis-par-45-straujaka-izaugsme-nelaimes-gadijumu-apdrosinasanai.a633433/

OCTA 2025 (LTAB release 15 Jan 2026, official, read by the skeptic): 35,617 road accidents reported to insurers (2024: 34,571), EUR 80.19m compensation decisions, average EUR 1,762 per decision (2024: 1,693). EUR 58.68m of the total was vehicle damage. Average claims are small, so the battery matters only in the tail. No powertrain split exists.

EV fleet: about 12,991 passenger EVs (1.6% of cars) on 1 Oct 2025 per LSM (26 Oct 2025, secondary; primary CSDD figure not verified). The team's 13,900 at end 2025 is not independently verified. Sources range from 10,458 to 12,991. Cite CSDD directly before the pitch. Used EVs were 22.9% of used cars registered in Jan 2025 (Auto Asociacija via LSM); the underlying counts were inconsistent.

Latvian insurer stance: LAA (survey of 1,010 residents, May 2025) says the EV CASCO price gap has narrowed or disappeared and that a separate battery deductible may apply. No insurer is named and no claims data is given. I found no Latvian insurer (BTA, Balta, If, ERGO, Compensa, Gjensidige, Seesam) statement on EV total losses, no battery write-off threshold and no tender. [searched, not found]

Fires: VUGD registered 523 vehicle fires in 2025 (2024: about 559; 2023: about 623), 397 of them passenger cars, with no EV split [official via lvportals.lv, 22 Oct 2026]. LAA chief (LSM 27 Dec 2025): 600-700 burned vehicle units a year, about one-third reach insurers, about 90% older than 5 years and about 90% diesel; new EVs rarely burn without a specific cause or a severe crash. VUGD has no published procedure for crashed EVs that I found.

Rules: Latvian ELV rules (MK 135, MK 748, MK 896) as found do not address EV traction batteries. This is a gap in what I could read, not proof of absence. Loss assessment is governed by LTAB-certified experts and its methodology. I found no source on how traction-battery damage is assessed in Latvia, no named EV-capable loss adjuster and no Baltic salvage auction data. LSM (Feb 2025) reports workshops lack hybrid and EV mechanics.

Estonia: Swedbank's risk insurance head (ERR, 14 Feb 2024) says the battery is often nearly half of a car's value; cases with OEM-mandated replacement after airbag deployment exceed EUR 50,000 and some reach EUR 85,000 (single insurer, no claim counts). The Kia Niro EUR 15,000 excluding battery and the 10 mm dent range come from Finnish outlet Moottori, not Swedbank. 7,834 electric-drive vehicles on 1 Nov 2024 (Transpordiamet via ERR).

Lithuania: 3,150 new BEVs registered in 2025 (EAFO). PalyginkDraudima.lt (Aug 2026) says BTA, Compensa and Lietuvos draudimas publish a separate EV parts depreciation table. The vehicle-fire figure of 845 comes from an unverified news site. Compensa says battery defects are covered by manufacturer warranty, not insurance.

Nordic and Finnish comparison (context): TV4 (18 Apr 2023) puts a new battery at SEK 100,000-300,000 with many OEMs disallowing repair. Norway write-off threshold: the industry moved from 60% to 80% of value around autumn 2021, not EV-specific (Bytt.no; skeptic says the single formulation 'Gjensidige, If and Fremtind 80%' is wrong for Gjensidige and If). If stopped Finnish CASCO for Taycan and e-tron GT in Jan 2024 and later reversed this conditionally (Moottori, 20 Mar 2024). Do not use the Finland EV total-loss figure of 8% to 10.2%; it could not be verified.

Competitor coverage: AVILOO warranty excludes all three Baltic states; Copart has no Baltic yards (Finland nearest, via AVK); Audatex Baltics UAB is in Vilnius (claims estimating only). So the field is open locally, but also untested, because no demand evidence exists.
buyer_map: Insurer CASCO claims head or head of motor claims (BTA, Balta, If, ERGO, Compensa, Gjensidige, Seesam): the economic buyer and the person who bears the loss. Pays for towing, storage, expert and repair or write-off under CASCO. Needs a verdict they can defend to the claimant and the reinsurer. They hold the claim files we need for the retrospective review.

Insurer technical or fraud/claims quality team and reinsurer: gatekeepers on liability. They will ask who pays if a cleared pack later burns. The TWAICE/Great Lakes accuracy guarantee is the precedent for insurer-backed assurance.

LTAB and LAA: the association and the OCTA bureau. LTAB certifies experts and holds the loss-assessment methodology. Useful as a credibility route and to understand whether our output can enter an expert report. Not a payer.

Independent loss adjusters and certified experts: they write the report that insurers rely on. Either a competitor for the assessment role or a distribution channel if we supply the battery data. Name of any EV-capable firm in Latvia: not found.

Tow and recovery firms: first on scene and decide pack removal, container use and storage. They invoice the insurer (Allianz EV tow cost about double; Koblenz and Harz cases). A natural distribution partner and also a cost the insurer wants cut. Latvian firms with EV procedures: not found.
Storage yards and body shops: hold the car during quarantine and repair. Need HV-qualified staff. Workshops in Latvia lack hybrid and EV mechanics (LSM, Feb 2025).
OEM importers and dealers: hold the diagnostic tools and the repair-instruction access. The dealer diagnostic is likely binding for warranty and liability. A partner if cooperative, a blocker if not.

Salvage dealers, importers and auction platforms: buy written-off cars and packs. No Baltic salvage data found. Buyers who benefit from a condition certificate; also potential suppliers of packs to our chain.
Leasing and fleet operators: own many young EVs, care about residual value, and are an adjacent buyer for SoH and post-incident certificates. (Not researched in detail.)
VUGD (fire and rescue): not a payer. Sets safety practice at the scene; no EV post-crash procedure found. A stakeholder to involve for credibility.
legal_safety_data_issues: Liability is the central issue. A 'safe to store or repair' verdict that is later followed by a fire exposes the assessor. A repair-shop owner told Reuters that insurers will not take the later-lawsuit risk (Reuters via devdiscourse, 20 Mar 2023; one quote). We need professional indemnity cover, a clearly limited scope ('no gross damage found at time of test', never 'safe'), and a contract that makes the insurer or expert the decision-maker. Whether PI cover exists for this risk in Latvia is unresearched.

The SVV annex is a voluntary industry guideline (section 2 of the annex says so), not law. It says its thresholds are averages and OEM instructions prevail. Do not present the 10 mm threshold as a legal or insurer rule in the pitch.

OEM instructions and warranty: OEM repair procedures may mandate replacement regardless of a third-party scan (AZT 14 Dec 2023). Doing HV work contrary to OEM procedure may void warranty and shift liability.

Insurance law principle: the injured party is owed restoration of the original condition, so even cosmetic casing damage can force a large-part replacement because casing repairs are not approved (AZT PDF, Jan 2023). A scan does not change this unless the OEM approves the repair.

Safety of the assessor: live HV work needs HV3 per the SVV annex; the minimum for scene work is HV1 plus HV2. We need qualified technicians and a safe site for a pack that could ignite later. Delayed re-ignition frequency is not known (not found).

Transport and storage of damaged packs: damaged or defective lithium batteries fall under special carriage rules (ADR) and are likely hazardous waste when written off. This is general knowledge, not in the research; check ADR requirements and Latvian waste permits before handling any pack. The Swiss annex covers extra disposal costs for significantly damaged packs (ChemRRV), which is Swiss law and not applicable to Latvia. Latvian ELV rules (MK 135, 748, 896) as found do not address HV batteries.

Data protection: VIN, plate, location, claim details and BMS or EDR data link to a person, so GDPR applies (my analysis, not researched). We need a data processing agreement with the insurer and a lawful basis. Who owns the BMS data (driver, OEM, insurer) is unsettled; Allianz argues battery data is the new odometer (Allianz press release 17 Oct 2023). The EU Battery Regulation passport starts Feb 2027 with SoH visible to persons with a legitimate interest, but insurer access is unconfirmed in the sources I read.

Independence and conflict of interest: an assessor paid by the insurer, who also buys written-off packs, has a conflict. If we advise 'write off' and then buy the pack for our chain, expect challenges from claimants and insurers. Need a separation of roles and disclosure.

Cost-of-quarantine disputes: courts scrutinise storage and quarantine fees. LG Koblenz cut a EUR 38,569.81 claim to EUR 7,596.96 total storage, and a Norwegian FinKN decision shows insurers must document causation. Our reports need to document the timeline and chain of custody to be useful as evidence.

Unverified figures in the team brief: the German GRS tariffs of EUR 1.44/kg NMC and EUR 4.38/kg LFP could not be reproduced from any GRS price sheet I could access. Treat as unverified until someone reads the current GRS tariff. The SVV date 'Feb 2026' is wrong (signed 31 Oct 2025, posted Mar 2026).
fit_with_our_battery_chain: Routing of packs the scan rejects: under the SVV criteria, packs with casing deformation of 10 mm or more, holes, water or fire involvement are excluded from further testing and disposed of. Those go to recycling or specialist handling, not second life. That is a feedstock and handling revenue line for us, but it is a cost centre for the insurer, so we must show we lower total cost. GRS tariffs for damaged packs (EUR 1.44/kg NMC, EUR 4.38/kg LFP, transport-critical packs in a safety container) are from the team brief and unverified.

Second life and salvage: only packs that pass the electrical and structural checks can be reused. The Synetiq claim that at least 95% of cells in stored packs are undamaged is a company estimate for its yard, so do not use it to size the second-life feedstock. Salvage uplift from a certified condition report is plausible but has no supporting data.

Take-back: insurer write-offs are a source of packs with known history, but only a small one. At the central volume of about 57 triggered assessments a year in Latvia, only a fraction of those are write-offs with a usable pack. Do not model the chain's supply on this stream.

Testing capability reuse: our battery health testing (EUR 60-130 per car in Riga, team data) uses the same BMS/OBD read-out as the electrical step of the SVV analysis. The incremental investment is HV safety qualification, an insulation tester, a safe holding site and the insurer interface.

Safe storage: a quarantine and holding yard for damaged packs, with fire-safe layout (UK 15 m and Swiss 2.5 m rules vary), is the scarce resource in the UK (a yard for 100 ICE cars holds about 2 quarantined EVs). A small purpose-built holding site could be the real asset. No Baltic equivalent found.
Conflict risk (repeated): being both the assessor for the insurer and the buyer of packs needs a clear separation.

Positioning: this is a service line that opens doors to insurers and tow firms and feeds the chain, not the main profit pool. It should be pitched as an entry channel with a pilot to prove value, not as the core revenue.
synthesis.pilot_with_an_insurer: ["GOAL: test two hypotheses in 8-10 weeks with one Latvian insurer. H1: a standard post-crash protocol (SVV-style) gives a decision the insurer would use in a measurable share of cases. H2: that decision saves more than it costs. The volume problem is the main design constraint. At about 57 triggered cases a year market-wide (own estimate), one insurer with a 20-30% share sees only 2-3 live cases in 8 weeks. So the pilot must combine a retrospective review with a live, low-volume prospective arm.", "PARTNER PROFILE: an insurer with a CASCO book that includes imports and young EVs, a claims head willing to share anonymised claim files, and a tow partner. Candidates to approach (none contacted): BTA, Balta, If, ERGO, Compensa, Gjensidige. Do not name one in the pitch as a partner.", "WEEKS 0-2 SETUP: data-sharing and confidentiality agreement; protocol written from the SVV annex (non-destructive, two stages) with OEM instructions as the override; technician with HV2/HV3 qualification or a certified partner; BMS/OBD reader and insulation tester; PI cover quote; agree definitions and the trigger (airbag deployed, underbody or casing impact, car towed from scene, hybrid and PHEV included to raise volume).", "WEEKS 2-4 RETROSPECTIVE ARM: the insurer provides 20-40 anonymised EV and hybrid claim files from the last 24 months with cost lines (tow, storage, expert, repair or write-off, battery cost). We review blind and record where the protocol would have changed a decision and what it would have cost. This gives the first sourced Latvian data on battery share and cost distribution, which does not exist publicly today.", "WEEKS 3-9 PROSPECTIVE ARM: every triggered EV claim at the insurer is assessed within 24 h of the tow. Exterior only, so a floor for any inspection-style product, not for battery assessment. https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-atho6z47gymk2 [vendor, 2026]

Consumer or dealer SoH test: AVILOO Premium EUR 99 (ecomento, undated); OeAMTC AVILOO Flash EUR 69 (vendor page, accessed Oct 2026); ADAC/ecomento-type guides EUR 100-150 [trade press / vendor]. Riga: EUR 60-130 per car (team data); a Latvian used-EV guide gives EUR 30-80 for a manufacturer-level SoH reading (wheelstreet.lt, not an insurer price).
Post-crash HV diagnosis: 'Lite' EUR 150-300 and 1-2 h; 'Full' 2-3 working days (elektronik-zeit.de, 11 Oct 2026, AI-assisted blog, unsourced; low confidence). No official or vendor price found.

Expert and special services in tow cases: battery expert EUR 1,650, pre-transport consultation about EUR 1,700, battery removal and storage box EUR 2,450 net (Spiegel e-208 case via auto-motor-und-sport.de, 4 Mar 2026; one anecdote).

Quarantine and storage rates: EUR 95/day claimed and EUR 76.16/day days 1-5 then EUR 19.04/day awarded (LG Koblenz, 4 May 2026); more than EUR 100/day (Harz case, firmenauto.de 21 Jan 2026); GBP 60 per 48 h extra cost per claim (Thatcham 2023).
What an avoided outcome is worth: pack replacement EUR 13,300-43,300 (AZT, 2021 claims); casing swap EUR 1,100-2,200; battery damage overall from under EUR 1,000 to EUR 29,000 (AZT, 10 Aug 2026).
Insurer-backed assurance precedent: TWAICE's accuracy guarantee pays 8 times the analytics price if outside guaranteed accuracy (electrive 12 Dec 2022).

Our proposal [own estimate]: EUR 150-250 per mobile assessment, or EUR 80-120 at a fixed site, or a shared-savings model (for example 10-15% of verified avoided cost). The central estimated gross saving is about EUR 435 per assessed claim, so a price above about EUR 200 leaves the insurer little net in the central case and loses money in the low case.
Not found: any insurer-paid price for a post-crash battery assessment. All the anchors above are adjacent.
risks: Demand risk: no insurer was found paying anyone for this today, and no pilot or measured saving was found. The pain is documented in the UK and Germany but not in Latvia.
Volume risk: about 57 triggered assessments a year in Latvia (own estimate) and a few hundred in the Baltics. The AZT '2% of claims' rests on about 8 cases from 2021.
OEM substitution: OEMs publish their own assessment criteria (the VW MEB catalogue) and hold diagnostic access. Their verdict is likely binding, which can make a third-party scan redundant.
Detection and liability risk: no scan can prove a pack safe. A single post-clearance fire could end the business. PI cover availability and cost unknown.
Standards risk: Thatcham/BSI, TUV-Verband, VDA and SVV are building the standards. Incumbents (DEKRA, TUV) will own the method in the large markets. We are an unproven entrant with no accreditation.
Shrinking cost pool: OEM 24 h quarantine, VDA/GDV/ADAC guideline and court caps are already cutting excess quarantine and tow cost, the best-documented saving.
Price pressure: Thatcham wants open, cheap diagnostics on common equipment, and insurers already pay for expert and workshop diagnostics. A premium price needs proof of avoided cost.

Data-quality risk in our own evidence: several headline numbers are secondary, old or contradicted (AZT 2021 sample, 18% higher AZT claim cost unverified, CCC 23.1% comparison misleading, Finland total-loss figure unverified, Norway threshold wrong in detail, the team's SVV date and GRS tariffs unverified). Using them in a pitch invites challenge.
Conflict of interest between assessing for insurers and buying packs for our chain.
Operational risk: we would handle damaged packs (fire risk, permits, storage space, HV-qualified staff) with a small team.
Customer concentration: Latvia has few insurers, so losing one pilot partner removes a large share of the market. Concentration also helps sales, but both effects are strong.
next_steps: Before the pitch (Sun 1 Nov 2026, 12:30): present the idea as a hypothesis with a pilot, not as proven savings. Remove or correct unverified figures (SVV 'Feb 2026' and 'escalation', GRS EUR 1.44/4.38 per kg, Finland total-loss share, the 18% AZT figure, CCC 23.1%). Lead with the EUR 13,300-43,300 vs EUR 1,100-2,200 AZT contrast, the 2% / 7% finding with its n=8 caveat, the quarantine and tow evidence, and the gap that nobody sells this.

Days 1-3: read the SVV annex PDF yourself (pages 9-11 are tables rendered as images and were not machine-readable) and the TUV-Verband whitepaper and VDA/ZDK guideline. Confirm the primary CSDD EV count for end 2025.

Days 1-5: list 6-8 Latvian contacts (insurer claims heads, LTAB, LAA, 2 tow firms, 1 expert firm, 1 OEM importer). Send a short interview request. Ask each: how many EV claims with possible battery involvement per year, what happens at the scene, what a quarantine day costs, who decides, would a third-party verdict be accepted.

Days 3-7: run 4-6 interviews. Priority questions are in the human-questions list. Record real numbers (claims per year, tow and storage invoices, dealer diagnostic fees) to replace the assumptions in the value estimate.

Days 5-10: draft the pilot agreement (data, confidentiality, scope, no-liability wording) and the one-page protocol based on the SVV annex. Get a quote for PI cover and for HV3 training or a qualified partner.
Days 7-12: cost one mobile assessment end to end (time, tools, travel, insurance) and replace the EUR 120-200 assumption.

Days 10-14: update the value estimate with interview data; decide go or no-go on a pilot, or pivot the pitch to the broader damaged-pack handling and routing service. Write the result into docs/ with every figure sourced, as the repo rule requires.
In parallel: contact one salvage or storage operator and one battery recycler for a quote on damaged-pack handling, to verify the GRS tariffs and the routing cost.
questions_that_need_a_human: Can the team get an introduction to a claims head at a Latvian insurer (BTA, Balta, If, ERGO, Compensa, Gjensidige), and will one share anonymised EV claim files? Without this the pilot cannot start.

How many EV claims per year with possible battery involvement does a Latvian insurer actually see, and what does a typical one cost in tow, storage, expert and repair? This replaces the 57-per-year estimate and the EUR 435 central value.
In practice, who decides at the scene in Latvia (police, VUGD, tow driver, insurer hotline), and do tow firms remove HV batteries or use containers? What do they charge per day to store a crashed EV?
Do Latvian insurers follow the OEM dealer diagnostic as binding, and would they ever accept an independent verdict that differs from it?
What does PI cover for an HV battery verdict cost, and is it available at all in Latvia? Who on the team holds, or can get, HV2/HV3 qualifications?
What are the Latvian permit and transport rules for storing and moving damaged lithium batteries (ADR, waste classification)? A legal check is needed; the research did not cover it.
Does the team prefer to build a services business (assessment, storage, routing) or a technology/data product? The evidence favours services in Latvia and data/standards play only in larger markets.
What is the minimum price and margin the team accepts per assessment, and is a shared-savings model acceptable?
Is the team willing to accept the conflict of interest of assessing for insurers and buying packs, or should the assessment be kept independent of the chain?
Which primary source supports the team's figure of about 13,900 EVs at end 2025 (CSDD)? The best verifiable figure I found is 12,991 at 1 Oct 2025.
Where did the GRS tariffs of EUR 1.44/kg NMC and EUR 4.38/kg LFP come from? I could not reproduce them from any GRS document I could access.
